title: feat: behaviour recall, a smaller start file and visuals
headline: The recall gate also grades what sessions do, the always-loaded rules file is 14% smaller under a lower cap, a PR or release whose measured cost moved shows it in a checked Visuals section, a branch gets one sweep, and the guards hold destructive local git while passing plain reads.
alignment: v1.42.0 is build 16 of the v2.0 plan: step T10's recall part and the rest of T9's byte diet, with the open guard and audit rows.

items.text: Behaviour recall: 14 tasks run in seeded throwaway folders, and a script grades what each session did (its tool calls, in order), beside the wording gate; a rule change records a behaviour line, and a run resumes after a crash.
The recall gate fails a rule change whose scored commit is missing, or whose graded text changed after the commit the run scored.

Three sections of the always-loaded rules file moved word for word to the rule files that load when they apply, and the use check fails a filled `AGENTS.md` over the new 25,000-byte cap, counted on disk.
Sessions compact at 400K, set in the project settings; the use check fails a compact window outside 100K to 400K, and an automatic compact writes the resume packet in time.
A closeout that ends its task marks the resume packet closed and, in a command-line session, ends with the one command to type; a resumed session whose task is closed is told to start fresh.
Sweep reviewers run on the mid model unless a role names one; security and the novel lens stay on the top model, and every high finding is re-checked there.
One sweep per branch: a re-sweep contract is refused with no override, and the fix check is each fix's failing-first test plus CI's test check, defined once.

The guard holds a local git act that throws away uncommitted or unpushed work (a hard reset, a forced checkout, switch or branch delete, a restore over changes, a stash drop, a reflog expire) until the owner's yes.
The guards pass a simple loop of reads and a `sed` line range, and still hold a loop that could write a guarded file.
The PR body audits pass a tool word inside a path or command in a code span; a bare tool word in a code span still fails.
The project launcher reads capital classes, a bracket set with a comma, chained and quoted climbs and large globs within its time limit, and names the project each reaches.
A reinstall puts back a changed user tool with a backup instead of skipping it, a project's local overlay is merged once and then left alone, and the merge hint quotes a path with a space.
A delete after a glued climb (`cd..`, `cd\`) is read as outside the project.
A recall run names every read outside its probe and the user config folder, grades the kit scripts and the behaviour suite with the rules, and measures a candidate's own skills and role files.

A PR body or release note whose measured tokens, the file sizes behind them, or a measured wait moved carries a Visuals section: the outcome first (dollars, time or window room), a chart and a table the audits recompute.
A session whose folder is given by its short name holds a write through a link into `.claude` or `.git`, and a user config folder under its own name keeps its settings file behind the owner's yes.
A delete after a bare-name cd waits when CDPATH may be set, in the command, the environment or a sourced file.
The project launcher names the project a climb through a link reaches, where bash lands rather than where the link sits.
The kit's privacy scan reads a committed PNG by its text chunks instead of failing it as non-ASCII.
A destructive git command whose subcommand is held in a variable waits behind a shell keyword (then, do, else, if, while, until, coproc) or an assignment, as it already did when it came first.

decisions.decision: Behaviour recall runs beside the wording gate, not in place of it
decisions.why: The wording gate stays until the owner locks the behaviour suite as its replacement; both lines are recorded for every rule change.

decisions.decision: Behaviour sessions may only read and load skills
decisions.why: An allowed interpreter beside an allowed write would run anything a session writes on the owner's PC; denied tool calls are still recorded and graded.

decisions.decision: The fix check is each fix's failing-first test plus CI, and no reviewer re-reads the fixes
decisions.why: The owner's one-sweep ruling: the failing-first test catches a half-done fix, and a second pass is the owner's call.

decisions.decision: Visuals shows numbers now, with a chart image only once committed
decisions.why: A typed number names the two commits it was measured at, so a later PR cannot repeat this one's saving; images follow in a later build.

verification: Each code change was seen failing on the code before it and passing after.
The start-up load was measured by `/context` on fresh installs of 1.41.0 and this branch.
upgrading: Run `install user` first, then `install project` in each project. A project's settings gain `autoCompactWindow: 400000`.
limits: The behaviour suite runs beside the wording gate and grades the project rules only. The released 1.41.0 fails the closeout task: a session ran the closeout steps by hand and never loaded the closeout skill. The guards do not read git aliases already in the owner's own config, or a CDPATH set by an interactive shell's startup files. The scored and behaviour lines are the lead's record; the reports behind them stay local.

visuals.summary: Visuals: the always-loaded rules file 27,609 B to 23,834 B (cap 25,000 B)
visuals.body:
<details>
<summary>Visuals: Always-loaded rules file 27,609 B to 23,834 B (cap 25,000 B)</summary>

Every session starts with 1,100 fewer tokens: about $4.40 less per 1,000 sessions at the uncached input price,
and 4.33 points more of the window used at start (the window went from 650,000 to 400,000 tokens).

![Chart: Always-loaded rules file 27,609 B to 23,834 B; Always-loaded rules file: tokens read at each session start 9,800 to 8,500; Always-loaded rules file: cost per 1,000 sessions $39.20 to $34.00; Whole start-up load 47,900 to 46,800; Whole start-up load: cost per 1,000 sessions $191.60 to $187.20; Whole start-up load: share of the window used at start 7.37% to 11.70%](https://github.com/GoudyMT/working-methodology/raw/138edcbc2aef5d86f793b177ac2ef718bf8dda14/docs/visuals/feat/behaviour-recall-and-diet/chart.png)

```text
Always-loaded rules file, bytes (| = limit 25,000)
before  ####################################|###  27,609
after   ################################### |     23,834
```

| Metric | Before | After | Change | Limit | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Always-loaded rules file | 27,609 B | 23,834 B | -3,775 B (-13.7%) | 25,000 B | measured: bytes at 83ab095 and 8dc1583 |
| Always-loaded rules file: tokens read at each session start | 9,800 | 8,500 | -1,300 (-13.3%) | none | measured: session context report, to 0.1k (docs/evals/results/e4-start-load.md) |
| Always-loaded rules file: cost per 1,000 sessions | $39.20 | $34.00 | -$5.20 (-13.3%) | none | derived: tokens x $4 per million input tokens, uncached (2026-11-03) |
| Whole start-up load | 47,900 | 46,800 | -1,100 (-2.3%) | none | measured: session context report, to 0.1k (docs/evals/results/e4-start-load.md) |
| Whole start-up load: cost per 1,000 sessions | $191.60 | $187.20 | -$4.40 (-2.3%) | none | derived: tokens x $4 per million input tokens, uncached (2026-11-03) |
| Whole start-up load: share of the window used at start | 7.37% | 11.70% | +4.33 points | none | derived: tokens / the window at each commit (650,000, then 400,000) |

**Why each number moved**

- **Always-loaded rules file:** three sections moved word for word to the rule files that load when their work
  starts.
- **Always-loaded rules file: tokens read at each session start:** follows from the Always-loaded rules file
  size.
- **Always-loaded rules file: cost per 1,000 sessions:** follows from tokens at the uncached input price;
  cached reads cost less.
- **Whole start-up load:** the rules file cut, offset in part by other start-up text; each count is rounded to
  0.1k.
- **Whole start-up load: cost per 1,000 sessions:** follows from tokens at the uncached input price; cached
  reads cost less.
- **Whole start-up load: share of the window used at start:** more of the window goes to the start, so less is
  left for the work before the session compacts; the window itself went from 650,000 to 400,000 tokens.
</details>
